To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce SilhoNet, a novel method that uses an intermediate representation to simultaneously estimate object pose and find viable grasp points, (2) our method outperforms PoseCNN on YCB-video dataset for 3D object pose estimation, and (3) SilhoNet is a step toward bridging the gap between 3D pose and grasp estimation.
we propose a novel method for RGB-only 3D pose and grasp estimation.
SilhoNet is an RGB-only method that predicts a 3D object pose and grasp points from a monocular RGB input, and that SilhoNet achieves better overall performance for 3D object estimation than PoseCNN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two contributions.
the development of a method for 3D object pose estimation and grasp point selection that can be performed in real-time with only RGB camera data.
the following questions: 1) Can we estimate 3D object pose and select a viable grasp point simultaneously using only monocular camera data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is a significant improvement over PoseCNN for 3D object pose estimation, and it can be used to select grasp points for a variety of objects.
our SilhoNet method achieves better performance than state-of-the art methods for both 3D pose prediction and grasp point selection.
SilhoNet is a novel method for 3D object pose estimation and grasp planning that achieves better overall performance on the YCB-Video dataset than state-of-the art methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method that uses only a monocular camera and is able to estimate the object pose, and also generate viable grasp points in a single pass.
we present a new method for RGB-based 3D pose and grasp point estimation.
we are the first to show that the problem of grasp point selection and object pose estimation can be solved simultaneously using only a monocular camera.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intermediate silhouette representation is a useful intermediate representation to bridge the gap between the problems of object pose estimation, and grasp point selection, and that the two problems should be solved together.
a single RGB image is sufficient for both object pose estimation and grasp point selection.

by jointly solving the problem of 3D pose prediction and grasp point selection, we can achieve better performance than solving these problems separately, and we do so with a simple and computationally efficient pipeline.
